messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Estimating only the item parameters
parts:
Hi Caio,

If you have the original data then what is stopping you from estimating the item parameter directly via mirt()? Again, I would advise against using previously saved point estimates since these are a) sub-optimal, in that they are either positively or negatively biased, and b) do not account for the sampling/measurement precision that was originally present (this is actually the main problem with a selection of item-fit statistics that rely on point estimates). No doubt if your estimation is the same as the original calibration then you'd be able to obtain the same latent trait point estimates anyway as a consequence, rendering your current point estimates redundant anyway. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Estimating only the item parameters
parts:
Hi Caio,

I see your problem. However, using the point estimates of the latent traits as provisionally known certainly won't give you the original item parameter estimates (it's not synonymous to a back-transformation operation). You'd likely get very different parameter estimates since the individual point estimates will have a very different mean/variance combination than the original calibration method (most likely mean-variance = 0-1). If you have multiple set of plausible values for the latent traits (which in some sense 'retain' the original identification constraints) then those could do a better job when averaged over, but even here they won't be perfect. IN any event, using only the subset data that you have available will likely give you much closer representations to the original data than any set of latent trait point estimates since the data are (presumably) both random samples from the same population. 

Phil
